answer:
Dear Jo,

I'd like to introduce the big yellow umbrella beside our school gate. On wet afternoons the guard uses it to walk students from the gate to the bus stop. I'd start with the snap of its catch, then record rain tapping on the fabric as two pairs of shoes walk together. Just before the bus pulls up, a student could call, “Mind your head while I fold it!” That should help our listeners guess what has kept those footsteps dry.

Yours,
Li Hua

answer:
I picked up the roll and called May over. I taped the paper beside the marks, with its bottom touching the floor. “Hold it there.” Each time May pointed to a line, I copied it across, name and date and all. She drew the shaky red one herself. Dad called from the stairs just as I reached my blue line. May rolled up the paper and carried it out under her raincoat.

That evening, Dad found us in the kitchen of our new flat. May had her heel on the paper to keep its bottom flat while I taped the top to the wall. She stood beside the lowest mark, then stretched towards the next. Dad took a pencil from behind his ear. “Heels down, please.” He drew a fresh line over her yellow hood. She pulled the hood off. “Again, Dad. That bit isn't me.”

wait patiently和wait impatiently均符合构词与句法。‘Even a short message takes time’既可接耐心等候也可接不耐烦，文中未给态度证据。建议认可两种或补一个不催促的细节。
